invariants: A fixed 200ms default window copies pending events; concurrent flush calls share a quiescence barrier.
Failed batches retain order; automatic retries pause until new admission or explicit flush. JSONL and SQLite roll back failed append batches.
Live events are serialized per ID and bound to an exact Session; teardown closes listeners before awaiting all writes and closing the backend.
HMR adopts only matching cwd and stored event prefixes, repairs byte tails without synthesizing interrupted-turn closers, and persists each seed/suffix once.
Retirement drains the old Session before a replacement claims its ID; cancellation of a Python flush observer does not cancel durability.
identity: Live state is keyed by exact Session object; owners, locks and retiring jobs are indexed by ID. Cold shared preparation reservations are not implemented by this layer.
ownership: LivePersistence owns initialization tasks, write controllers and retirement jobs. Cordis owns listener cleanup and the final drain. Both storage plugins use the same coordinator.
ordering: Initialize/adopt prefix -> persist seed -> queued suffix; same-ID lock serializes live writes. Concurrent flush reaches quiescence including admitted tails. Backend close follows all drains, even on failure.
errors: Background failures are reported with retained batches; explicit flush rejects. Mismatched cwd/prefix rejects without overwriting the artifact. SQLite transaction and JSONL truncate/fsync restore old append prefix after write failure.
cancellation: Consumer awaits shared barriers through asyncio.shield; cancelling one observer does not cancel initialization or write tasks. Cross-process writer exclusion and shared preparation observer cancellation are outside this contract.
adaptation: Python 3.8 call_later implements bounded batching and settled empty flush is synchronous. Local deterministic clock probes cover source write-behind cases; four paired real upstream JSONL journeys compare type/seq/data and rejection boolean (generated timestamps and diagnostic wording are not compared). SQLite runs the same local lifecycle matrix; upstream SQLite native-module parity is not claimed.
